  requires (acc >= 0)
  ensures (result >= 0)
  ensures ((len(xs) > 0) or (result == acc))
  effects pure
  example (balance_from([], 5) == 5)
  example (balance_from([-5, 2], 0) == 2)
  example (balance_from([10, -3, -20, 5], 0) == 12)
{
  match xs { [] => acc [h, ..t] => if ((h < 0) and ((acc + h) < 0)) then balance_from(t, acc) else balance_from(t, (acc + h)) }
}

fn balance(xs: List[Int]) -> Int
  requires forall x in xs: (x != 0)
  ensures (result >= 0)
  ensures (result == balance_from(xs, 0))
  effects pure
  example (balance([10, -3, -20, 5]) == 12)
  example (balance([-5, 2]) == 2)
  example (balance([]) == 0)
{
  balance_from(xs, 0)
}

  ensures (result == len(xs))
  effects pure

fn nth(xs: List[Int], i: Int) -> Int
  requires ((i >= 0) and (i < len(xs)))
  ensures (result == xs[i])
  effects pure
  example (nth([1, 4, 6, 9], 0) == 1)
  example (nth([1, 4, 6, 9], 2) == 6)
{
  match xs { [] => 0 [h, ..t] => if (i == 0) then h else nth(t, (i - 1)) }
}

fn bs(xs: List[Int], x: Int, lo: Int, hi: Int) -> Option[Int]
  requires (sorted(xs) and distinct(xs))
  requires (((lo >= 0) and (lo <= hi)) and (hi <= len(xs)))
  ensures ((result != None) or (forall i in lo..hi: (xs[i] != x)))
  ensures forall i in lo..hi: ((xs[i] != x) or (result == Some(i)))
  ensures forall i in 0..len(xs): ((result != Some(i)) or ((i >= lo) and (i < hi)))
  effects pure
  example (bs([1, 4, 6, 9], 6, 0, 4) == Some(2))
  example (bs([1, 4, 6, 9], 5, 0, 4) == None)
  example (bs([], 3, 0, 0) == None)
{
  if (lo >= hi) then None else if (nth(xs, ((lo + hi) / 2)) == x) then Some(((lo + hi) / 2)) else if (nth(xs, ((lo + hi) / 2)) < x) then bs(xs, x, (((lo + hi) / 2) + 1), hi) else bs(xs, x, lo, ((lo + hi) / 2))
}

  requires (sorted(xs) and distinct(xs))
  ensures (contains(xs, x) or (result == None))

fn collatz_next(n: Int) -> Int
  requires (n >= 1)
  ensures ((((n % 2) == 0) and (result == (n / 2))) or (((n % 2) == 1) and (result == ((3 * n) + 1))))
  ensures (result >= 1)
  effects pure
  example (collatz_next(6) == 3)
  example (collatz_next(7) == 22)
  example (collatz_next(1) == 4)
{
  if ((n % 2) == 0) then (n / 2) else ((3 * n) + 1)
}

fn collatz_ok(n: Int, k: Int) -> Bool
  requires (n >= 1)
  ensures ((n != 1) or (result == (k == 0)))
  ensures ((not result) or (k >= 0))
  effects pure
  example (collatz_ok(1, 0) == true)
  example (collatz_ok(1, 1) == false)
  example (collatz_ok(6, 8) == true)
  example (collatz_ok(6, 7) == false)
  example (collatz_ok(6, 9) == false)
{
  if (n == 1) then (k == 0) else if (k <= 0) then false else collatz_ok(collatz_next(n), (k - 1))
}

  requires (n >= 1)

fn count_less(xs: List[Int], v: Int) -> Int
  requires (len(xs) >= 0)
  ensures ((result >= 0) and (result <= len(xs)))
  ensures ((result == 0) == (forall x in xs: (x >= v)))
  ensures ((result == len(xs)) == (forall x in xs: (x < v)))
  effects pure
  example (count_less([7, 2, 9, 4], 5) == 2)
  example (count_less([7, 2, 9, 4], 2) == 0)
  example (count_less([7, 2, 9, 4], 10) == 4)
  example (count_less([], 3) == 0)
{
  match xs { [] => 0 [h, ..t] => if (h < v) then (1 + count_less(t, v)) else count_less(t, v) }
}

fn min_or(xs: List[Int], d: Int) -> Int
  requires (len(xs) >= 0)
  ensures ((result == d) or contains(xs, result))
  ensures (result <= d)
  ensures forall x in xs: (result <= x)
  effects pure
  example (min_or([7, 2, 9, 4], 10) == 2)
  example (min_or([], 3) == 3)
  example (min_or([9, 8, 7], 1) == 1)
  example (min_or([5], 9) == 5)
{
  match xs { [] => d [h, ..t] => if (h < d) then min_or(t, h) else min_or(t, d) }
}

fn minimum(xs: List[Int]) -> Int
  requires (len(xs) >= 1)
  ensures contains(xs, result)
  ensures forall x in xs: (result <= x)
  effects pure
  example (minimum([7, 2, 9, 4]) == 2)
  example (minimum([5]) == 5)
  example (minimum([9, 8, 7]) == 7)
{
  match xs { [] => 0 [h, ..t] => min_or(t, h) }
}

fn remove(xs: List[Int], v: Int) -> List[Int]
  requires distinct(xs)
  requires contains(xs, v)
  ensures (len(result) == (len(xs) - 1))
  ensures not contains(result, v)
  ensures distinct(result)
  effects pure
  example (remove([7, 2, 9, 4], 2) == [7, 9, 4])
  example (remove([7, 2, 9, 4], 9) == [7, 2, 4])
  example (remove([5], 5) == [])
{
  match xs { [] => [] [h, ..t] => if (h == v) then t else ([h] ++ remove(t, v)) }
}

fn kth_smallest(xs: List[Int], k: Int) -> Int
  requires distinct(xs)
  requires ((k >= 1) and (k <= len(xs)))
  ensures contains(xs, result)
  ensures (count_less(xs, result) == (k - 1))
  effects pure
  example (kth_smallest([7, 2, 9, 4], 1) == 2)
  example (kth_smallest([7, 2, 9, 4], 3) == 7)
  example (kth_smallest([7, 2, 9, 4], 4) == 9)
  example (kth_smallest([5], 1) == 5)
{
  if (k == 1) then minimum(xs) else kth_smallest(remove(xs, minimum(xs)), (k - 1))
}
